author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Kioxia’s plan to list American depositary shares in the United States could broaden the Japanese memory-chip maker’s investor base and improve trading liquidity, according to a Voya Investment Management fund manager interviewed by Reuters. The company announced in May that it was preparing the U.S. listing; it has not yet completed the transaction.

Kioxia’s Tokyo-listed shares have risen 456% this year, reflecting intense investor interest in memory suppliers connected to artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Sebastian Thomas, who helps manage Voya’s $14 billion artificial-intelligence fund, said a U.S. listing could raise Kioxia’s global visibility.

Thomas said the fund does not currently own Kioxia. Voya’s AI strategy holds about $5 billion from Japanese investors but tends to favor larger, more liquid companies. Its semiconductor exposure includes South Korea’s SK Hynix and U.S.-based Micron.

A depositary-share listing would not change Kioxia’s underlying business, but it could make the stock easier for some U.S. institutions to access and compare with global peers. Execution, timing and investor demand remain uncertain until the company files final terms and completes the process. The share-performance figures are year-to-date data reported by Reuters, not live market quotes.
dek: The Japanese memory-chip maker is preparing an American depositary-share listing as fund managers emphasize liquidity and global visibility.
headline: Kioxia’s planned U.S. listing could widen AI-investor access
